Team — draft technical responses below (I kept each item short so we can paste into the questionnaire workbook):

1) NIST AI RMF mapping (high level):
- Identify: model inventory (served models + variants), input data taxonomy, model provenance tags (origin, weights, training data license). We maintain an internal model registry with immutable version metadata and hash IDs.
- Protect: access control via RBAC + mTLS, encryption at rest (KMS/HSM) and in transit, token-scoped rate limits, and VPC/private deployment options. For private deployments we offer customer-managed KMS.
- Detect: runtime anomaly detection (latency/score drift), telemetry hooks for per-request metadata, and continuous evaluation jobs that compare live outputs vs. baseline test vectors.
- Respond: automatic fallback to hardened model variants or cached responses, canary rollbacks with automatic routing and alerting to on-call. We keep deploy audit logs for each rollout.
- Recover: snapshot and redeploy previous model versions, automated warm-up of KV caches, and documented recovery runbooks.

2) EU AI Act positioning:
- We treat LLMs used for decision-making affecting legal/financial eligibility as potentially high-risk. For customers classifying their use as high-risk, we require Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with contractual assurances.
- Technical & organizational measures: data minimization, logging and traceability (per-request metadata retained per customer retention policy), human-in-the-loop review toggles, pre-deployment risk assessment tied to our model registry, provision of conformity packages (testing reports, documentation for conformity assessment).

3) Regression / eval approach (core):
- Baseline corpus: curated seed prompts, synthetic adversarial variations, and customer-supplied golden prompts where available. Corpus stored versioned in our eval bucket.
- Metrics: semantic similarity (BLEURT/Embedding cosine), factuality/regression score (ground-truth where available), toxicity and safety classifiers, latency and token-cost deltas.
- Frequency: nightly automated regression runs for hosted models; for Dedicated/Private, scheduled weekly by default with ad-hoc runs on model changes or config flips.
- Thresholds & alerts: per-model thresholds configurable per-customer; exceedance creates an incident in Jira SEC-4287 and triggers a canary or rollback depending on policy.
- Rollback workflow: automated routing to previous pinned model + on-call notification and an audit log entry. We also provide a snapshot of the failing run and diff report (CSV) for post-mortem.

Artifacts I can attach: sample regression summary CSV (redwood-eval-harness-summary-2026.csv), a sanitized runbook for rollback, and example per-customer threshold config.

Notes: for the EU Act high-risk flows we recommend Private deployment and signed SLA for retention and audit access. Happy to expand any bullet into a paragraph for legal.

— Marcus

Redwood Inference
